math.subject: math
math.summaryHe: The picture of the subject in mathematics: the child succeeds in composition over time. There is also room for reinforcement in comparing quantities or numbers.

stableExcellence.tierHe: Your child is doing well on this topic over time

math.parentActionHe: Three times a week, 15-20 minutes each session: choose one math task on the subject of comparing quantities or numbers - read the formulation together, formulate out loud what is given and what is requested, perform a first step on a draft sheet and only then write a final answer and check against the solution.
math.nextWeekGoalHe: Target for reinforcement: increase the Prozent of success in comparing quantities or numbers (at least one more successful attempt than last week). Goal for retention: continue a relaxed practice routine on composition to maintain the level of accuracy.

evidenceExamples.exerciseText: Wie viele bags is the price of the computer higher?

evidenceExamples.titleHe: What your child is doing well in practice
evidenceExamples.bodyHe: In the subject of essay there is good success in the selected period: about 93% correct out of 42 questions.

studentRecommendationsImprove.textHe: You should practice a little more on the subject: when comparing quantities or numbers - 7 similar mistakes were recorded in the selected period. We stay with focused practice and not with "trying to fix everything at once".

studentRecommendationsMaintain.textHe: Continue practicing comfortably on the topic of connection - the level there is maintained (accuracy about 93%).

parentRecommendationsImprove.textHe: A repetition of the same type of error begins - in the subject of comparing quantities or numbers. For the coming week, a calm look and a short, focused practice are enough.

parentRecommendationsMaintain.textHe: It is recommended to encourage persistence in connection - you see repeated success; Maintaining a positive habit is just as important as correcting mistakes.

geometry.subject: Geometrie
geometry.summaryHe: The overall picture in Geometrie: there is also room to strengthen recurring confusion between Umfang and area.

geometry.parentActionHe: Three times a week, 15–20 minutes each session: choose one Geometrie task on recurring confusion between Umfang and area — read the problem together, say out loud what is given and what is asked, take a first step on scrap paper, then write the final answer and check it.
geometry.nextWeekGoalHe: Practice goal: raise success on recurring confusion between Umfang and area (at least one more successful attempt than last week).
